missions.title: Side quest: The East Well
missions.knowledgeQuestion: Whose knowledge should shape a plan that affects a whole community?

objectives.title: Optional: listen to Efua Asante, the fruit seller and Hesper about the low well.
Optional: make a plan with Efua.
Optional: read the notched depth sticks at the east well and the west well.
Optional: tell Efua what you take from this.
Optional: show the guildmaster what you found.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Listen when the bucket lands. That second clack is the handle hitting stone. Last summer we never heard it. Now someone has written HESPER on the well cover. My sister took her kettle home empty.

options.text: Then I'll ask. What do you need?
I know what to do. Close the forge.
Not now.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Do you? You have not seen the well, met my neighbour, or asked the smith. Close the forge and Hesper loses her work, and maybe the well stays low. Ask first.

options.text: You're right. What do you need?
Later.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Water before the soup bell. And I want my sister to be able to fetch it without walking over somebody’s name. Ask the fruit seller what she saw. Hesper can tell you where she fills her barrel.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Have you heard the fruit seller and Hesper? Their reasons matter as much as mine.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: I’ve scraped the name off the lid. There’s still a pale H. We can leave the smithy working and keep a record, or take Hesper up on her three days. Which sheet shall I pin here?

options.text: Measure both wells at the same bell while Hesper works her usual shifts.
Take Hesper up on her offer to use less water for three days.
You decide. I'll just carry the buckets.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Carrying buckets is kind. But you've heard everyone, and that's useful. Help us choose.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: I’ll copy the marks from both wells at dawn. Hesper keeps her usual shifts. Take today’s reading at each stick so we know where our watch began.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Four notches below each well’s own summer mark. My sister heard that and asked when the rain would come. I wish the sticks could tell her. What do you want in the margin before I send these to Orrin?

options.text: Listening first told us which well feeds Hesper’s barrel.
Keep both summer marks. The same drop can have more than one cause.
The people who missed a turn at the bucket belong in this record too.
I’m not sure how much either the forge or the weather mattered.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Orrin has a hook for one covered jug at the hall. Take him the sticks and the sheet we picked. Someone needs to put water on that hook today.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: I still have the two sticks here. Orrin’s notice gives their readings. He’s kept a space below for the next person who gets here with an empty cup.

options.text: Leave the two sticks with Efua.
Choose a bell for tomorrow’s covered jug.

dialogue.speaker: fruit-seller
dialogue.text: I chalked the H. Just the H. I could see steam from Hesper’s roof and the bottom of my bucket in the same glance. I couldn’t see where she filled hers. My little one asked me who wrote the rest of her name.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: Two buckets from the west well go into my barrel. One for the morning heat, one for the last. I can do cold work for three days if we keep a count. After that someone is going to want their hinges.

dialogue.speaker: guildmaster-orrin
dialogue.text: I can fit both sticks on the notice. Four notches down from two summer marks. I had a line here naming the season. Pass me the scraper. What else did we actually see?

options.text: Unroll the three dawn entries with the usual forge shifts.
Show the three short-draw days and the rain-jar slip.
Lay the two dated stick readings on the desk.
Fold the sheet away for now.

dialogue.speaker: fruit-seller
dialogue.text: Fresh fruit from the river farms! Yellow, red, green. Prices on the boxes, no arguing today.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: I’ll hang the ladle upside down after my first bucket and leave the second on its peg. Start at the two depth sticks. Efua can put the rain jar out while I tell my apprentice why the hinges have to wait.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: Three dawns. East went four, five, five notches below its mark. West went four, four, five. Hesper drew her usual two buckets each day. We can show when the readings diverged. No one measured how much the other houses drew.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: Here’s the ladle tally. I drew one bucket each day. On the third morning both sticks stood one notch higher. Efua’s jar caught rain the night before. If you write that my cold forge raised the water, where will you put the rain?

dialogue.speaker: guildmaster-orrin
dialogue.text: We have one covered jug to set aside each day. The soup kettle needs it at dawn. The porters get here after the stalls have shut. I can keep it on the hook for either bell. Whose place am I keeping?

options.text: Hang it for the soup kettle at dawn.
Seal it for the porters at the closing bell.
Leave the jug on the desk while I think.

dialogue.speaker: well-keeper
dialogue.text: My sister gets the kettle over the fire before the children arrive. At closing I find a porter turning the lid round on its empty hook. He asks me to write down his bell too.

options.text: Keep the dawn hook.
Take the hook back to Orrin and change its bell.

dialogue.speaker: fruit-seller
dialogue.text: The porter came back expecting an empty hook. You should have seen him lift that lid. We served the broth late this morning. Tomorrow I’ll tell people before they queue.

options.text: Keep the closing-bell hook.
Take the hook back to Orrin and change its bell.

hints.text: Everyone has an answer. Who has been asked?
Three people care about the well.
Talk to Efua by the east well, the fruit seller by the fruit boxes, and Hesper at the forge.
Efua is by the well east of the square. The fruit seller stands near the fruit boxes south of the square. Hesper is at the forge in the west.
Make the plan with Efua, not for her.
Leaving the forge running lets you watch its ordinary days. Hesper’s other offer changes her draw.
Talk to Efua. Choose to keep watch or to take up Hesper’s offer.
Choose ‘Measure both wells’ for the watch. Choose ‘use less water’ for Hesper’s three-day trial.
Each well has a notched depth stick.
One stick is by Efua. The other is west, beyond the smithy.
Read the stick at the east well, then walk west past the forge to the west well.
Use the east well stick next to Efua, and the west well stick south-west of the forge.
What did the sticks show?
What would the sticks look like if more than one thing had lowered the water?
Talk to Efua and say what you take from it.
Talk to Efua. Pick the margin entry you want Orrin to read.
Orrin has room for both sticks on his notice and one jug on his hook.
Who speaks for the town?
Open the sheet for the plan you picked. Choose who can count on the covered jug.
At the guild hall, take Orrin through your record. Hang the jug for dawn or the closing bell.

journal.text: I put both of Emberford’s readings on Orrin’s desk. Each well was four notches below its own summer mark when we began. We could give someone a turn at the jug while we kept looking for the cause.
